svg.title: Predator synthetic search quality and joint5 instruction counts
svg.desc: Reported October 20, 2026 synthetic simulator and compilation tests, separate from the IBM Fez hardware pilot. The untuned circuit used one layer and 4,096 samples per run. Reported best-sample score gaps across three seeds: 6 candidates 0 to 11 percent, 8 candidates 6 to 15 percent, 16 candidates 28 to 41 percent, and 20 candidates 46 to 72 percent. Zero is best. joint5 routed instruction changes calculated from rounded mean counts: 12 candidates about 13 percent fewer, 16 about 7 percent fewer, 32 about 4 percent more, 40 about 14 percent more. There were three seeds at 12 and 16, two at 32, and one at 40. Ranges are observations, not confidence intervals. Selected sizes shown; full aggregates are in docs/research/search-scaling.json. These are synthetic scores and instruction counts, not mission success rates or run-time measurements. No quantum advantage or independent confirmation is established.
